subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram support an inherited forced-plain outbound mode beyond the existing standard-HTML and `richMessages` paths, and should raw HTML or MarkdownV2 remain out of scope?
rationale: The code can mechanically carry another mode, but maintainers must define the permanent config name, supported values, inheritance, default, and trust boundary rather than letting an implementation invent a public compatibility-sensitive contract.

options.title: Add Safe Plain Mode
options.body: Preserve standard HTML by default and add one inherited opt-in that sends escaped, unformatted plain text across all Telegram delivery paths.

options.title: Expose Multiple Parse Modes
options.body: Support plain, HTML, and MarkdownV2 only after defining raw-input trust, escaping, fallback, captions, previews, and account inheritance as a documented public contract.

options.title: Keep Existing Modes
options.body: Retain standard HTML plus the `richMessages` opt-in and close the request without adding another configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Add Safe Plain Mode
recommendation.body: Preserve standard HTML by default and add one inherited opt-in that sends escaped, unformatted plain text across all Telegram delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The HTML transition, recent issue review, and repeated Telegram configuration history make this the strongest available product-routing signal.
